title: Munozara va qarshi fikr bildirish
goal_uz: Dars oxirida munozarada gapni odob bilan bo‘lasiz, fikrga qisman rozi bo‘lib qarshi dalil keltirasiz, aniqlashtiruvchi savol berasiz va ikki pozitsiyani neytral xulosalaysiz.

scenes.title: Munozara san’ati
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda urg‘u, ohang va bog‘lanishni o‘rgandik. Bugun shu ohangni jonli munozarada ishlatamiz. Dars oxirida siz gapni odob bilan bo‘lasiz, fikrga qisman rozi bo‘lib qarshi chiqasiz, noaniq joyni so‘rab aniqlaysiz va ikki tomonning pozitsiyasini xulosalaysiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back. Last time we worked on stress and intonation. Today you will use them in a real debate: interrupting politely, conceding and countering, asking for clarification, and summing up both sides.
scenes.say_uz: Xush kelibsiz. Oldingi darsda urg‘u va ohang ustida ishladik. Bugun ularni haqiqiy munozarada qo‘llaymiz: odob bilan bo‘lish, tan olib qarshi chiqish, aniqlashtirish va ikki tomonni xulosalash.

scenes.title: Yaxshi munozara nima?
board: Attack the argument, never the person

examples.t: I disagree with the idea, not with you.
examples.uz: Men fikrga qarshiman, sizga emas.

scenes.say_native: Ingliz tilida “debate” fikrlar bahsi, maqsadi g‘oyani sinash. Kundalik nutqda “argument” esa ko‘pincha janjalga o‘xshaydi. Kuchli munozarachi baqirmaydi: u xotirjam, dalilli va hurmatli. Shuning uchun bugungi iboralar doim fikrga qaratiladi, shaxsga emas. Bu qoida o‘zbek majlislarida, ayniqsa kattalar bilan gaplashganda ham ishlaydi.
scenes.say: A good debate is not a quarrel. The aim is to test ideas, so we challenge the argument, never the person. The strongest speakers stay calm, give reasons and show respect.
scenes.say_uz: Yaxshi munozara janjal emas. Maqsad g‘oyalarni sinash, shuning uchun dalilga qarshi chiqamiz, shaxsga emas. Kuchli so‘zlovchi xotirjam bo‘ladi, sabab keltiradi va hurmat qiladi.

scenes.title: Gapni odob bilan bo‘lish
board: If I could just come in here...
Can I just stop you there?

examples.t: Sorry to interrupt, but could I make a quick point?
examples.uz: Bo‘lganim uchun uzr, bitta qisqa fikr aytsam bo‘ladimi?

examples.t: If I could just come in here for a second.
examples.uz: Bir soniya gapga qo‘shilsam.

scenes.say_native: Birinchi mavzu: gapni bo‘lish. O‘zbekchada “Gapingizni bo‘lganim uchun uzr” deymiz, inglizchada xuddi shu ma’noda “Sorry to interrupt, but”. Qat’iyroq, lekin hamon odobli variant: “Can I just stop you there?” Yig‘ilishlarda “If I could just come in here” tabiiy eshitiladi. Formula oddiy: uzr, sabab va ruxsat so‘rovi.
scenes.say: There are polite ways to cut in. Sorry to interrupt, but could I make a quick point? If I could just come in here for a second. Can I just stop you there? Each phrase asks permission instead of demanding the floor.
scenes.say_uz: Gapga kirishning odobli yo‘llari bor. Bo‘lganim uchun uzr, qisqa fikr aytsam bo‘ladimi? Bir soniya gapga qo‘shilsam. Shu yerda to‘xtatsam bo‘ladimi? Har bir ibora talab qilmaydi, ruxsat so‘raydi.

scenes.title: Kuch darajasi
board: Firm: Can I just stop you there?
Urgent: Sorry, I have to jump in.

examples.t: Sorry, I have to jump in: that figure isn’t correct.
examples.uz: Kechirasiz, aralashishim kerak: bu raqam noto‘g‘ri.

scenes.say_native: Bu iboralar kuchi bilan farq qiladi. “May I add something?” eng yumshoq, gap tugashiga yaqin aytiladi. “Sorry to interrupt, but” o‘rtacha. “Can I just stop you there?” qat’iy, gap noto‘g‘ri yo‘nalishda ketsa ishlatiladi. “Sorry, I have to jump in” esa muhim xatoni, masalan noto‘g‘ri raqamni, zudlik bilan tuzatish uchun.
scenes.say: Choose the strength to fit the moment. May I add something? is gentle. Sorry to interrupt, but is medium. Can I just stop you there? is firm. Sorry, I have to jump in is for urgent corrections.
scenes.say_uz: Kuchni vaziyatga moslang. May I add something? yumshoq. Sorry to interrupt, but o‘rtacha. Can I just stop you there? qat’iy. Sorry, I have to jump in shoshilinch tuzatish uchun.

scenes.title: Sizning gapingiz bo‘linsa
board: Let me just finish this point.
I’ll come to that in a moment.
Let me finish, then I’d love to hear you.

examples.t: Let me just finish this point, and then it’s your turn.
examples.uz: Shu fikrni tugatay, keyin sizning navbatingiz.

scenes.say_native: Teskari holat: sizning gapingiz bo‘linsa-chi? G‘azablanmang. Odobli javob: “Let me just finish this point”, ya’ni shu fikrni tugatay. Yoki “I’ll come to that in a moment”, bunga birozdan keyin keladi. Ohang iliq, ovoz ishonchli bo‘lsin. Shunda vaqtingizni himoya qilasiz va suhbatdoshni xafa qilmaysiz.
scenes.say: What if somebody interrupts you? Stay calm and keep the floor. Let me just finish this point, and then it's your turn. Or: I'll come to that in a moment.
scenes.say_uz: Sizning gapingiz bo‘linsa, xotirjam bo‘lib navbatni saqlang. Shu fikrni tugatay, keyin navbat sizniki. Yoki: bunga birozdan keyin keladi.

scenes.title: O‘zbekcha bilan solishtirish
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida kattaning gapini bo‘lish noqulay, shuning uchun ko‘pincha jim kutamiz. Inglizcha yig‘ilishlarda esa o‘z vaqtida qo‘shilish faollik belgisi, jim qolsangiz fikringiz yo‘qdek tuyulishi mumkin. Lekin faqat odobli shaklda. Ruscha “Подождите” ni so‘zma-so‘z “Wait!” deb tarjima qilsangiz, buyruqdek eshitiladi.
scenes.say: In many English-speaking meetings, joining in at the right moment shows you are engaged. But it only works in a polite form. A bare Wait! or Stop! sounds like an order.
scenes.say_uz: Ingliz yig‘ilishlarida o‘z vaqtida qo‘shilish faollikni bildiradi. Lekin faqat odobli shaklda. Yalang Wait! yoki Stop! buyruqdek eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Qo‘pol bo‘lish
board: ✓ Sorry to interrupt, but I’m not sure that’s right.
✓ Could I just come in here?
scenes.say_native: Shoshib qolgan o‘quvchilar ko‘pincha “Wait, wait! You are wrong!” deyishadi. Bu juda keskin, go‘yo suhbatdoshni ayblayotgandek. “Stop talking” ham shunday. To‘g‘risi: avval uzr, so‘ng yumshoq fikr: “I’m not sure that’s right”. “You’re wrong” o‘rniga “I’m not sure” yoki “I see it differently” munozarada ancha ta’sirli.
scenes.say: Avoid commands and direct accusations. Don't say, Wait! You're wrong! Say: Sorry to interrupt, but I'm not sure that's right. Or: Could I just come in here?
scenes.say_uz: Buyruq va to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri ayblovdan qoching. Wait! You're wrong! demang. Ayting: bo‘lganim uchun uzr, lekin bu to‘g‘ri deb o‘ylamayman. Yoki: gapga qo‘shilsam bo‘ladimi?

scenes.title: Mos iborani tanlang
board: 1) A friend talks for too long.
2) A manager gives a wrong date.
3) A speaker is finishing; you add a point.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uch vaziyat. Birinchi: do‘stingiz juda uzun gapiryapti, yumshoq qo‘shilmoqchisiz. Ikkinchi: menejer noto‘g‘ri sana aytdi. Uchinchi: so‘zlovchi tugatmoqda, siz qo‘shimcha qilmoqchisiz. Har biriga mos iborani baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Three situations. A friend talks for too long. A manager gives a wrong date. A speaker is finishing and you want to add something. What do you say each time?
scenes.say_uz: Uch vaziyat. Do‘st uzun gapiryapti. Menejer noto‘g‘ri sana aytdi. So‘zlovchi tugatmoqda, qo‘shmoqchisiz. Har safar nima deysiz?

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1) Sorry to interrupt, but could I make a point?
2) Sorry, I have to jump in. I think it’s the 14th.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Birinchisiga: “Sorry to interrupt, but could I make a point?”, o‘rtacha va do‘stona. Ikkinchisiga: “Sorry, I have to jump in”, chunki xato zudlik bilan tuzatilishi kerak, so‘ng sanani ayting. Uchinchisiga: “May I add something?”, eng yumshog‘i. Sizniki shunga yaqin bo‘lsa, ajoyib.
scenes.say: Possible answers. One, Sorry to interrupt, but could I make a point? Two, Sorry, I have to jump in, I think it's the fourteenth. Three, May I add something?
scenes.say_uz: Mumkin javoblar. Bir, bo‘lganim uchun uzr, bir fikr aytsam bo‘ladimi? Ikki, aralashishim kerak, menimcha o‘n to‘rtinchi. Uch, qo‘shimcha qilsam bo‘ladimi?

scenes.title: Tan olib, qarshi chiqish
board: I see where you’re coming from, but...

examples.t: That’s a fair point, but it doesn’t apply to small firms.
examples.uz: Bu o‘rinli fikr, lekin kichik firmalarga taalluqli emas.

examples.t: I see where you’re coming from, but the data says otherwise.
examples.uz: Nima demoqchi ekaningizni tushunaman, lekin ma’lumotlar boshqacha.

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu: concede and counter, ya’ni qisman tan olib, keyin qarshi dalil keltirish. Avval suhbatdoshning to‘g‘ri tomonini tan olasiz: “That’s a fair point”, “I take your point”. So‘ng “but” yoki “however” bilan o‘z dalilingizni aytasiz. Shunda siz adolatli tinglovchi bo‘lib ko‘rinasiz, dalilingiz esa ishonchliroq bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: The strongest move in a debate is to concede, then counter. First acknowledge what is valid: That's a fair point. Then add your own argument with but or however.
scenes.say_uz: Munozaradagi eng kuchli usul: avval tan olish, keyin qarshi chiqish. Avval to‘g‘ri tomonini tan oling: bu o‘rinli fikr. So‘ng but yoki however bilan o‘z dalilingizni qo‘shing.

scenes.title: While, admittedly, granted
board: While it’s true that X, Y.

examples.t: While it’s true that cars are convenient, they cause pollution.
examples.uz: Mashinalar qulay ekani rost, ammo ifloslanish keltiradi.

examples.t: Granted, it’s cheaper. However, the quality is lower.
examples.uz: Arzonroq ekani rost. Biroq sifati past.

scenes.say_native: Faqat “but” ni takrorlash zerikarli. Yetuk nutqda “While it’s true that…” — ...ekani rost, ammo. “Admittedly… Even so…” — tan olaman, shunday bo‘lsa-da. “Granted… However…” — aytaylik, rost, biroq. Tan olishni avval, asosiy fikringizni oxirida qo‘ying, chunki tinglovchi oxirgi qismni yaxshiroq eslab qoladi.
scenes.say: Vary your structures. While it's true that cars are convenient, they cause pollution. Admittedly, it's cheaper. Even so, the quality is lower. Put the concession first and your real point last.
scenes.say_uz: Tuzilmalarni almashtiring. Mashinalar qulay ekani rost, ammo ifloslantiradi. Tan olaman, arzonroq. Shunday bo‘lsa-da, sifati past. Tan olishni avval, asosiy fikrni oxirida qo‘ying.

scenes.title: Qarshi dalil turlari

examples.t: That would mean fewer jobs in the long run.
examples.uz: Bu uzoq muddatda ish o‘rinlari kamayishini bildiradi.

examples.t: A better option is to reduce, not ban.
examples.uz: Yaxshiroq yechim taqiqlash emas, kamaytirishdir.

scenes.say_native: “Yo‘q, siz noto‘g‘risiz” qarshi dalil emas. Kuchli qarshi dalil uch xil bo‘ladi. Isbot: “The figures show…”. Oqibat: “That would mean…”, bu shuni bildiradi. Muqobil: “A better option is…”. Har gal bittasini tanlang va qisqa asoslang. Faqat rad etmang, nimadir qo‘shing.
scenes.say: A counter-argument needs content. Use evidence: The figures show a fall in sales. Show a consequence: That would mean fewer jobs. Or offer an alternative: A better option is to reduce, not ban.
scenes.say_uz: Qarshi dalil mazmunli bo‘lsin. Isbot: raqamlar savdo tushganini ko‘rsatadi. Oqibat: bu ish o‘rinlari kamayishini bildiradi. Muqobil: yaxshiroq yechim taqiqlash emas, kamaytirishdir.

scenes.title: Although ... but
board: ✗ Although it is expensive, but it works.
✓ Although it is expensive, it works.
✓ It is expensive, but it works.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilidan o‘tadigan klassik xato. Biz “garchi qimmat bo‘lsa-da, lekin ishlaydi” deymiz va ikkita bog‘lovchi ishlatamiz. Ingliz tilida “although” va “but” bir gapda birga kelmaydi, faqat bittasi kerak. Yoki “Although it is expensive, it works”, yoki “It is expensive, but it works”. Xuddi shu qoida “despite” va “however” uchun ham o‘rinli.
scenes.say: A common mistake from Uzbek: using although and but together. Say: Although it is expensive, it works. Or: It is expensive, but it works. Never both in one sentence.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbek tilidan o‘tadigan xato: although va but ni birga ishlatish. To‘g‘risi: Although it is expensive, it works. Yoki: It is expensive, but it works. Bir gapda ikkalasi emas.

scenes.title: Tan oling va qarshi chiqing
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uch fikr berilgan. Har biriga avval tan oling, keyin qarshi dalil keltiring. Masalan: “Granted, cars are convenient, but…” deb ifloslanish yoki tirbandlik haqida davom eting. Har safar boshqa tuzilma ishlating. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Three statements. Concede first, then counter. Cars are very convenient. Online classes are cheaper. Social media connects people. Use a different structure each time.
scenes.say_uz: Uch fikr. Avval tan oling, keyin qarshi chiqing. Mashinalar qulay. Onlayn darslar arzonroq. Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar odamlarni bog‘laydi. Har safar boshqa tuzilma.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javoblar
board: 1) Granted, cars are convenient, but they cause pollution.
2) While it’s true they’re cheaper, students lose face-to-face contact.
3) Admittedly, it connects people. Even so, it can isolate them.
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “Granted, cars are convenient, but they cause pollution.” Ikkinchi: “While it’s true that online classes are cheaper, students lose face-to-face contact.” Uchinchi: “Admittedly, social media connects people. Even so, it can leave them feeling isolated.” Tekshiring: tan olish bormi, qarshi dalil aniqmi, although bilan but aralashib ketmadimi?
scenes.say: Model answers. Granted, cars are convenient, but they cause pollution. While it's true that online classes are cheaper, students lose face-to-face contact. Admittedly, social media connects people. Even so, it can leave them feeling isolated.
scenes.say_uz: Namunalar. Mashinalar qulay, lekin ifloslantiradi. Onlayn darslar arzonroq ekani rost, ammo talabalar yuzma-yuz aloqani yo‘qotadi. Tarmoqlar bog‘laydi, shunday bo‘lsa-da, yolg‘izlantirishi mumkin.

scenes.title: Aniqlashtirish so‘rash
board: Could you clarify what you mean by...?
When you say X, do you mean...?
Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that.

examples.t: When you say “cheap”, do you mean low-quality?
examples.uz: “Arzon” deganda sifatsiz degani nazarda tutilyaptimi?

examples.t: Are you saying that all students should pay?
examples.uz: Hamma talabalar to‘lashi kerak demoqchimisiz?

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu: aniqlashtirish. Fikr noaniq bo‘lsa, tushunmay turib javob bermang. “Could you clarify what you mean by…?” — nimani nazarda tutasiz? “When you say X, do you mean…?” — X deganda... degani nazarda tutilyaptimi? “Are you saying that…?” — ...demoqchimisiz? Eshitmay qolsangiz: “Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that”.
scenes.say: Don't argue against something you haven't understood. Could you clarify what you mean by sustainable? When you say cheap, do you mean low-quality? And if you missed it: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that.
scenes.say_uz: Tushunmagan narsangizga qarshi chiqmang. Barqaror deganda nimani nazarda tutasiz? Arzon deganda sifatsiz degani nazarda tutilyaptimi? Eshitmasangiz: kechirasiz, to‘liq eshitmadim.

scenes.title: So what you’re saying is...
board: So what you’re saying is that...
Let me check I’ve got this right.

examples.t: If I understand you correctly, you want to ban all cars.
examples.uz: Sizni to‘g‘ri tushunsam, barcha mashinalarni taqiqlamoqchisiz.

examples.t: So what you’re saying is that fees should rise?
examples.uz: Demak, to‘lovlar oshishi kerak demoqchisiz?

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi usul: suhbatdosh fikrini o‘z so‘zingiz bilan qaytarish, ya’ni paraphrase. “If I understand you correctly, …”, “So what you’re saying is that…”. Bu xato tushunishdan saqlaydi va suhbatdoshga fikrini aniqlashtirish imkonini beradi. Siz hukm chiqarmayapsiz, faqat tekshiryapsiz, shuning uchun ohang oxirida ko‘tariladi.
scenes.say: A second technique is to paraphrase. If I understand you correctly, you want to ban all cars. So what you're saying is that fees should rise? Let me check I've got this right.
scenes.say_uz: Ikkinchi usul: o‘z so‘zingiz bilan qaytarish. Sizni to‘g‘ri tushunsam, barcha mashinalarni taqiqlamoqchisiz. Demak, to‘lovlar oshishi kerak demoqchisiz? To‘g‘ri tushunganimni tekshirib olay.

scenes.title: Ohang munozarada
board: I see your point ↗, but...  (gap tugamadi)

examples.t: Are you saying that ↗ all students should pay?
examples.uz: Hamma talabalar to‘lashi kerak demoqchimisiz?

scenes.say_native: Oldingi darsga qaytamiz: ohang munosabatni bildiradi. Aniqlashtiruvchi savol oxirida ko‘tariladi. Qat’iy fikr pasayuvchi ohang bilan aytiladi. “I see your point, but…” da “point” dan keyingi ko‘tarilish gap hali tugamaganini bildiradi. Xotirjam, tekis ovoz tanqidni yumshatadi, baland va tez gapirish esa munozarani janjalga o‘xshatadi.
scenes.say: Intonation carries attitude. A clarifying question rises: Are you saying that all students should pay? A firm statement falls. A small rise before but in I see your point, but, tells us you have not finished.
scenes.say_uz: Ohang munosabatni bildiradi. Aniqlashtiruvchi savol ko‘tariladi. Qat’iy fikr pasayadi. I see your point, but da but oldidagi kichik ko‘tarilish gap tugamaganini bildiradi.

scenes.title: Noto‘g‘ri aniqlashtirish
board: ✓ Sorry, could you say that again?
scenes.say_native: Ikki xato. Birinchi: “What do you mean?” ni qattiq ohangda aytish, bu “nima deb valdirayapsan” kabi eshitilishi mumkin. Yaxshisi: “What do you mean by fair?” — aniq so‘zga qaratilgan. Ikkinchi: “Repeat!” deb buyruq berish, bu ruscha “Повторите” dan so‘zma-so‘z o‘tadi. To‘g‘risi: “Sorry, could you say that again?”
scenes.say: Be careful with tone. What do you mean?! can sound hostile. Try: What do you mean by fair? And don't command: Repeat! Say, Sorry, could you say that again?
scenes.say_uz: Ohangga ehtiyot bo‘ling. What do you mean?! dushmanona eshitilishi mumkin. Yaxshisi: adolatli deganda nimani nazarda tutasiz? Buyruq bermang: kechirasiz, yana ayta olasizmi?

scenes.title: Savol bering
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uch noaniq gap. Har biriga bitta aniqlashtiruvchi savol bering. Birinchisida “modern” noaniq. Ikkinchisida “everyone” va “bad”. Uchinchisida qaysi qoidalar? Masalan: “When you say modern, do you mean…?” Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Three vague statements. Ask one clarifying question for each. Schools should be more modern. Social media is bad for everyone. We need stronger rules.
scenes.say_uz: Uch noaniq gap. Har biriga bitta aniqlashtiruvchi savol bering. Maktablar zamonaviyroq bo‘lsin. Ijtimoiy tarmoq hamma uchun yomon. Bizga qattiqroq qoidalar kerak.

scenes.title: Mumkin savollar
board: 1) When you say “modern”, do you mean more technology?
2) Do you mean it’s bad for everyone, even adults?
3) Which rules are you thinking of?
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “When you say modern, do you mean more technology?” Ikkinchi: “Are you saying it’s bad for absolutely everyone, including adults?” Uchinchi: “Could you clarify which rules you have in mind?” Har safar noaniq so‘zni aniqlayapmiz. Noaniq da’vo ko‘pincha aniq savol oldida zaiflashadi.
scenes.say: Possible questions. When you say modern, do you mean more technology? Are you saying it's bad for absolutely everyone, including adults? Could you clarify which rules you have in mind?
scenes.say_uz: Mumkin savollar. Zamonaviy deganda texnologiya ko‘pligini nazarda tutasizmi? Hamma uchun, kattalar uchun ham yomon demoqchimisiz? Qaysi qoidalarni nazarda tutyapsiz?

scenes.title: Tinglang: to‘rt kunlik ish haftasi
board: Anna: A four-day week boosts productivity.
Mark: Sorry to interrupt, but what do you mean by productivity?
Mark: Fair point, but staff may burn out.
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialog. Anna va Mark to‘rt kunlik ish haftasini muhokama qiladi. Tinglang: Mark gapni qanday bo‘ladi, nimani aniqlashtiradi va Annaning gapiga qanday javob beradi.
scenes.say: Anna: A four-day week boosts productivity. Mark: Sorry to interrupt, but what do you mean by productivity? Anna: Output per hour. People work better when they're rested. Mark: That's a fair point, but if they pack five days into four, some will burn out. Anna: Not in the trials I've read about.
scenes.say_uz: Anna: To‘rt kunlik hafta samaradorlikni oshiradi. Mark: Bo‘lganim uchun uzr, samaradorlik deganda nimani nazarda tutasiz? Anna: Soatiga chiqim. Odamlar dam olsa yaxshiroq ishlaydi. Mark: Bu o‘rinli fikr, lekin besh kunlik ishni to‘rtga sig‘dirsa, ba’zilari charchab qoladi. Anna: Men o‘qigan tajribalarda unday emas.

scenes.title: Dialogni tekshiring
board: 2) What does he ask Anna to clarify?
scenes.say_native: Uchta savol. Birinchi: Mark gapni qaysi ibora bilan bo‘ldi? Ikkinchi: u nimani aniqlashtirishni so‘radi? Uchinchi: qaysi ibora Annaning gapini tan oldi va keyin qarshi dalil keltirdi? O‘zingiz ayting.
scenes.say: Three questions. How does Mark interrupt? What does he ask Anna to clarify? Which phrase concedes a point before the counter-argument?
scenes.say_uz: Uch savol. Mark gapni qanday bo‘ladi? Nimani aniqlashtirishni so‘raydi? Qaysi ibora fikrni tan oladi?

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: Mark “Sorry to interrupt, but” dedi. Ikki: u “productivity” so‘zini so‘radi, Anna “output per hour” deb aniq javob berdi. Uch: “That’s a fair point, but” — Mark tan oldi, keyin charchash dalilini keltirdi. Anna ham xotirjam qoldi va o‘z manbasiga tayandi.
scenes.say: Answers. One, Sorry to interrupt, but. Two, the word productivity; Anna defines it as output per hour. Three, That's a fair point, but. Anna stays calm and refers to evidence.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar. Bir, bo‘lganim uchun uzr, lekin. Ikki, productivity so‘zi; Anna uni soatiga chiqim deb aniqlaydi. Uch, bu o‘rinli fikr, lekin. Anna xotirjam qoladi va dalilga tayanadi.

scenes.title: Pozitsiyalarni xulosalash
board: We agree that..., but we differ on...
The main point of disagreement is...

examples.t: To sum up, Anna favours the change, while Mark has concerns.
examples.uz: Xulosa qilsak, Anna o‘zgarishni qo‘llaydi, Markda xavotir bor.

scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu: summarising positions. Munozara cho‘zilganda yoki oxirida xulosa qilinadi. Tuzilma oddiy: nimada rozimiz, nimada farq qilamiz, asosiy tortishuv nima. “To sum up, …”, “We agree that …, but we differ on …”, “The main point of disagreement is …”. Xulosa neytral bo‘lsin, o‘z fikringizni yashirincha qo‘shmang.
scenes.say: Summing up shows leadership. State what we agree on, where we differ, and the main point of disagreement. To sum up, Anna favours the change, while Mark has concerns.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosalash yetakchilikni ko‘rsatadi. Nimada roziligimiz, nimada farqimiz va asosiy tortishuv. Xulosa qilsak, Anna o‘zgarishni qo‘llaydi, Markda xavotir bor.

scenes.title: Fikrni ifodalovchi fe’llar

examples.t: Anna argues that shorter weeks raise output.
examples.uz: Anna qisqa haftalar samaradorlikni oshiradi, deb dalil keltiradi.

examples.t: Mark is concerned that staff will burn out.
examples.uz: Mark xodimlar charchab qolishidan xavotirda.

scenes.say_native: Birovning fikrini bayon qilishda “said” dan boshqa fe’llar kerak. “Argue” — dalil bilan da’vo qilish. “Claim” — isbotlanmagan bo‘lishi mumkin bo‘lgan da’vo. “Maintain” — fikrda qat’iy turish. “Point out” — e’tiborni qaratish. Ularning hammasidan keyin “that” va to‘liq gap keladi.
scenes.say: Use reporting verbs. Argue means to give reasons. Claim suggests something not yet proven. Maintain means to hold a view firmly. Anna argues that shorter weeks raise output. Mark is concerned that staff will burn out.
scenes.say_uz: Fe’llardan foydalaning. Argue sabab keltirish. Claim hali isbotlanmagan da’vo. Maintain fikrda qat’iy turish. Anna qisqa haftalar samaradorlikni oshiradi deb dalil keltiradi. Mark xodimlar charchashidan xavotirda.

scenes.title: Boshqaruvchi iboralari
board: Can I summarise where we are?
Let me check I’ve understood your position.
Let’s hear from the other side.

examples.t: Can I summarise where we are before we move on?
examples.uz: Davom etishdan oldin hozirgi holatni xulosalab olsam bo‘ladimi?

scenes.say_native: Xulosani munozara o‘rtasida ham qilish mumkin. “Can I summarise where we are?” — hozirgi holatni xulosalab olsam. “Let me check I’ve understood your position” — pozitsiyangizni to‘g‘ri tushunganimni tekshirib olay. “Let’s hear from the other side” — boshqa tomonni eshitaylik. Bu iboralar munozarani tartibga soladi va ikkala tomonni hurmat qiladi.
scenes.say: A summary also helps in the middle of a discussion. Can I summarise where we are before we move on? Let me check I've understood your position. Let's hear from the other side.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosa munozara o‘rtasida ham foydali. Davom etishdan oldin holatni xulosalab olsam bo‘ladimi? Pozitsiyangizni to‘g‘ri tushunganimni tekshirib olay. Boshqa tomonni eshitaylik.

scenes.title: Xulosadagi xatolar
board: ✗ Anna told that homework is useless.
✓ Anna said / argued that homework is useless.
scenes.say_native: Ikki xato. Birinchi: “told that”. “Tell” dan keyin odam kerak: “Anna told me that…”. Odamsiz “said that” yoki “argued that” ishlating. Ikkinchi: uchinchi shaxs birlikda -s tushib qolishi, “Mark think”. To‘g‘risi “Mark thinks”. Va yana bir qoida: xulosada “Anna is right” demang, chunki xulosa neytral bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: Two frequent errors. Tell needs a person: Anna told me that homework is useless, but Anna said that homework is useless. And keep the third-person s: Mark thinks it is bad.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki xato. Tell dan keyin odam kerak: Anna menga dedi, lekin Anna said that. Uchinchi shaxs s ni unutmang: Mark thinks it is bad.

scenes.title: Ikki pozitsiyani xulosalang
board: Lena: Homework causes stress and steals family time.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Sam uy vazifasi yaxshi odatlarni shakllantiradi deydi. Lena esa uy vazifasi stress keltiradi va oila vaqtini oladi deydi. Ikki gapda xulosa qiling: birinchi gapda ikki pozitsiya, ikkinchi gapda asosiy tortishuv. Argues va is concerned that fe’llarini ishlating.
scenes.say: Sam says homework builds good habits. Lena says it causes stress and steals family time. Summarise both positions in two sentences, using a reporting verb.
scenes.say_uz: Sam uy vazifasi yaxshi odat shakllantiradi deydi. Lena u stress keltiradi va oila vaqtini oladi deydi. Ikki gapda xulosa qiling.

scenes.title: Xulosa namunasi
board: Sam argues that homework builds good habits, while Lena is concerned that it causes stress.
The main point of disagreement is whether the benefits outweigh the cost.
scenes.say_native: Namuna: “Sam argues that homework builds good habits, while Lena is concerned that it causes stress and takes time from the family. The main point of disagreement is whether the benefits outweigh that cost.” “While” ikki pozitsiyani bir gapda tenglashtirdi, ikkinchi gap asosiy tortishuvni ko‘rsatdi. Hech kim haq deb e’lon qilinmadi.
scenes.say: A model summary. Sam argues that homework builds good habits, while Lena is concerned that it causes stress and takes time from the family. The main point of disagreement is whether the benefits outweigh that cost.
scenes.say_uz: Namuna. Sam uy vazifasi yaxshi odat shakllantiradi deb dalil keltiradi, Lena esa u stress keltirishi va oiladan vaqt olishidan xavotirda. Asosiy tortishuv: foyda bu zarardan ustunmi.

scenes.title: Tinglang: shahar markazi
board: Host: Should cars be banned from city centres?
Tom: I take your point, but shops would lose customers.
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog — radio munozara. Boshlovchi, Priya va Tom shahar markazidan mashinalarni taqiqlash haqida gaplashadi. Tom qanday qo‘shilishiga, Priya qanday so‘rashiga va boshlovchi qanday xulosa qilishiga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: Host: Should cars be banned from city centres? Priya: Yes. The air would be cleaner. Tom: May I add something? I take your point, but shops would lose customers. Priya: When you say lose, do you mean permanently? Tom: Many would close. Host: To sum up, Priya stresses health, while Tom is worried about local business.
scenes.say_uz: Boshlovchi: Markazdan mashinalar taqiqlansinmi? Priya: Ha, havo toza bo‘ladi. Tom: Qo‘shimcha qilsam bo‘ladimi? Fikringizni tushunaman, lekin do‘konlar mijoz yo‘qotadi. Priya: Yo‘qotadi deganda abadiy nazarda tutilyaptimi? Tom: Ko‘plari yopiladi. Boshlovchi: Priya salomatlikni ta’kidlaydi, Tom mahalliy biznesdan xavotirda.

scenes.title: Yana tekshiring
board: 3) What does Priya ask Tom to clarify?
scenes.say_native: Uch savol. Birinchi: kim taqiqni xohlaydi va nima uchun? Ikkinchi: Tomning qarshi dalili nima? Uchinchi: Priya Tomdan nimani aniqlashtirishni so‘raydi? Javobni ayting.
scenes.say: Three questions. Who wants the ban, and why? What is Tom's counter-argument? What does Priya ask Tom to clarify?
scenes.say_uz: Uch savol. Kim taqiqni xohlaydi va nima uchun? Tomning qarshi dalili nima? Priya nimani aniqlashtiradi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar. Bir: taqiqni Priya xohlaydi, chunki havo toza bo‘ladi. Ikki: Tom “I take your point, but” deb tan olib, keyin do‘konlar mijoz yo‘qotishini aytadi. Uch: Priya “lose” so‘zini aniqlashtiradi: abadiymi? Boshlovchi esa qisqa va adolatli xulosa qildi.
scenes.say: Answers. Priya wants the ban because the air would be cleaner. Tom says shops would lose customers. Priya asks whether lose means permanently. The host closes with a short, fair summary.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar. Priya taqiqni xohlaydi, chunki havo toza bo‘ladi. Tom do‘konlar mijoz yo‘qotishini aytadi. Priya lose abadiymi, deb so‘raydi. Boshlovchi qisqa, adolatli xulosa qiladi.

scenes.title: Bir nutq tuzilmasi
board: I believe... because... For instance... So...

examples.t: I believe cities should limit cars because pollution harms children.
examples.uz: Menimcha, shaharlar mashinalarni cheklashi kerak, chunki ifloslanish bolalarga zarar qiladi.

scenes.say_native: Uch daqiqalik munozara uchun har bir nutqingizga tuzilma kerak: da’vo, sabab, misol, qaytish. “I believe that … because … For instance, … So …”. Misol: shaharlar mashinalarni cheklashi kerak, chunki ifloslanish bolalarga zarar qiladi. Masalan, ba’zi joylarda markaz yopilgach, havo yaxshilangan. Demak, taklif oqilona. Har nutq 30–40 soniya bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: For a three-minute debate, give each turn a shape: claim, reason, example, link back. I believe cities should limit cars because pollution harms children. For instance, air quality improved in some places after centres closed to traffic. So the proposal is reasonable.
scenes.say_uz: Har nutqqa shakl bering: da’vo, sabab, misol, qaytish. Shaharlar mashinalarni cheklashi kerak, chunki ifloslanish bolalarga zarar qiladi. Masalan, ba’zi joylarda havo yaxshilangan. Demak, taklif oqilona.

scenes.title: Mutlaq so‘zlarni yumshating
board: ✓ I’m afraid I see it differently.
✓ I’d say that’s only partly true.

examples.t: I’m not convinced that a ban would work.
examples.uz: Taqiq ishlashiga ishonchim komil emas.

scenes.say_native: “You’re totally wrong” yoki “It’s obvious” ohangni qattiqlashtiradi va tinglovchini mudofaaga o‘tkazadi. Uning o‘rniga “I’m not convinced that…”, “I’m afraid I see it differently” yoki “I’d say that’s only partly true” deng. Rad etishingiz aniq qoladi, hurmat esa saqlanadi.
scenes.say: Soften disagreement without weakening it. Instead of You're totally wrong, say I'm not convinced that a ban would work. Or: I'm afraid I see it differently. Or: I'd say that's only partly true.
scenes.say_uz: Rad etishni zaiflashtirmasdan yumshating. You're totally wrong o‘rniga: taqiq ishlashiga ishonchim komil emas. Yoki: afsuski, men boshqacha qarayman. Yoki: bu faqat qisman to‘g‘ri.

scenes.title: Yumshatib qayta ayting
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uchta qo‘pol gapni ma’nosini saqlagan holda hurmatli qilib qayta ayting. Yordam: I’m not convinced, I see it differently, I’m not sure everyone would agree. Baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Three blunt statements. Rewrite each one so it is firm but respectful. That's a stupid idea. You're completely wrong. Nobody wants that.
scenes.say_uz: Uch qo‘pol gap. Har birini qat’iy, lekin hurmatli qiling. Bu ahmoqona fikr. Siz mutlaqo noto‘g‘risiz. Buni hech kim xohlamaydi.

scenes.title: Yumshoq variantlar
board: 1) I’m not convinced that idea would work.
2) I’m afraid I see it quite differently.
3) I’m not sure everyone would want that.
scenes.say_native: Namunalar. Birinchi: “I’m not convinced that idea would work.” Ikkinchi: “I’m afraid I see it quite differently.” Uchinchi: “I’m not sure everyone would want that.” Uchinchisida “nobody” ni “not everyone” ga almashtirdik. Nobody, everyone, always, never kabi mutlaq so‘zlarni rad etish oson, shuning uchun ehtiyotkor ifoda kuchliroq.
scenes.say: Model answers. I'm not convinced that idea would work. I'm afraid I see it quite differently. I'm not sure everyone would want that. We replaced nobody with not everyone, because absolute words are easy to challenge.
scenes.say_uz: Namunalar. Bu fikr ishlashiga ishonchim komil emas. Afsuski, men butunlay boshqacha qarayman. Hamma buni xohlashiga ishonchim komil emas. Mutlaq so‘zlarni rad etish oson.

scenes.title: Tayyorgarlik
board: Pick a side: claim, reason, example
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy topshiriqqa tayyorlanamiz. Mavzu: uy vazifasi taqiqlanishi kerak. Tomon tanlang va qisqa reja tuzing: da’vo, sabab, misol. Qarshi tomon nima deyishini ham o‘ylab qo‘ying. Faqat kalit so‘zlar yozing.
scenes.say: Time to prepare. The motion is: Homework should be banned. Choose a side and plan a claim, a reason and an example. Think what the other side might say.
scenes.say_uz: Tayyorlanish vaqti. Mavzu: uy vazifasi taqiqlanishi kerak. Tomon tanlab, da’vo, sabab va misolni rejalang. Qarshi tomon nima deyishini o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Namunaviy nutq
board: I’m not convinced homework should be banned.
While it’s true that it causes stress, it builds habits.
To sum up, the problem is quantity.
scenes.say_native: Namuna: “I’m not convinced homework should be banned. While it’s true that it can cause stress, it also builds study habits that last. Ten minutes of reading a night improves vocabulary. A better option is less homework, not none. To sum up, the problem is quantity, not the idea.” Yumshoq rad etish, tan olish, misol, muqobil va xulosa — bir daqiqadan kam.
scenes.say: A model turn. I'm not convinced homework should be banned. While it's true that it can cause stress, it also builds study habits that last. A better option is less homework, not none. To sum up, the problem is quantity, not the idea.
scenes.say_uz: Namunaviy nutq. Uy vazifasi taqiqlanishiga ishonchim komil emas. U stress keltirishi rost, lekin saqlanadigan o‘qish odatlarini ham shakllantiradi. Yaxshiroq yechim vazifani kamaytirish. Xulosa: muammo miqdorda, g‘oyada emas.

scenes.title: Mini-munozara
scenes.say_native: Navbat sizda. Uy vazifasi mavzusida gapiring. Tan olish va qarshi dalil, xayoliy raqibga bitta aniqlashtiruvchi savol va bir gapli xulosa kiriting. Keyin qarama-qarshi tomondan takrorlang. Xatodan qo‘rqmay, to‘xtamasdan gapiring.
scenes.say: Your turn. Speak about homework. Include a concession and counter, one clarifying question to an imaginary opponent, and a one-sentence summary. Then switch sides and repeat.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizda. Uy vazifasi haqida gapiring. Tan olish va qarshi dalil, bitta aniqlashtiruvchi savol, bir gapli xulosa. Keyin tomonni almashtiring.

scenes.title: O‘zingizni baholang
scenes.say_native: Beshta savol bilan baholang. Gapni odob bilan bo‘ldingizmi? Avval tan olib, keyin qarshi chiqdingizmi? Aniqlashtiruvchi savol berdingizmi? Xulosa neytral bo‘ldimi? Ohang xotirjam va hurmatli bo‘ldimi? Yetishmaganini qayta mashq qiling, takrorlash ravonlikni oshiradi.
scenes.say: Check yourself. Did you interrupt politely? Did you concede before countering? Did you ask a clarifying question? Was your summary neutral? Was your tone calm and respectful?
scenes.say_uz: O‘zingizni tekshiring. Odob bilan bo‘ldingizmi? Avval tan olib qarshi chiqdingizmi? Aniqlashtirdingizmi? Xulosa neytralmi? Ohang xotirjam va hurmatlimi?

scenes.title: Dars xulosasi
board: Clarify: When you say X, do you mean...?
scenes.say_native: Takrorlaymiz. Bo‘lish: “Sorry to interrupt, but”. Tan olish va qarshi chiqish: “That’s a fair point, but”, “While it’s true that”. Aniqlashtirish: “When you say X, do you mean…?”. Xulosalash: “To sum up”, “The main point of disagreement is”. Xatolar: although bilan but birga kelmaydi, tell dan keyin odam kerak, shaxsga hujum qilmang.
scenes.say: Let's recap. To interrupt: Sorry to interrupt, but. To concede and counter: That's a fair point, but. To clarify: When you say X, do you mean? To summarise: To sum up. Aim at the argument, never the person.
scenes.say_uz: Takrorlaymiz. Bo‘lish: bo‘lganim uchun uzr, lekin. Tan olib qarshi chiqish: bu o‘rinli fikr, lekin. Aniqlashtirish: X deganda nimani nazarda tutasiz? Xulosa: xulosa qilsak. Shaxsga emas, dalilga qarshi chiqing.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Record it and check the list
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifangiz: o‘qituvchi bergan mavzulardan birida uch daqiqalik munozara o‘tkazing va yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: bitta odobli bo‘lish, ikkita tan olib qarshi chiqish, bitta aniqlashtiruvchi savol va oxirida neytral xulosa. Keyingi darsda taxmin va ehtimollikni ifodalashni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: For homework, hold a three-minute debate on one of the teacher's prompts and record it. Include a polite interruption, two concede-and-counter moves, a clarifying question and a neutral summary. Next time: speculation and probability.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: o‘qituvchi mavzularidan birida uch daqiqalik munozara qiling va yozib oling. Odobli bo‘lish, ikki tan olib qarshi chiqish, aniqlashtirish va neytral xulosa bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda: taxmin va ehtimollik.

homework_uz: O‘qituvchi bergan mavzulardan birida uch daqiqalik munozara o‘tkazing va yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: bitta odobli bo‘lish, ikkita tan olib qarshi chiqish, bitta aniqlashtiruvchi savol va oxirida neytral xulosa.

quiz.q: Which is the most polite way to interrupt?
options: Sorry to interrupt, but could I make a point?
quiz.why_uz: Uzr, sabab va ruxsat so‘rovi eng odobli shakl.

options: Although it is expensive, but it works.
Although it is expensive, it works.
Although it is expensive but, it works.
quiz.why_uz: Although va but bir gapda birga kelmaydi; o‘zbekchadan o‘tadigan xato.

quiz.q: 'That's a fair point, but...' is an example of:
quiz.why_uz: Avval tan olinadi, keyin qarshi dalil keltiriladi.

options: When you say cheap, do you mean low-quality?
I don't care what you mean.
quiz.why_uz: When you say X, do you mean...? aniqlashtirish uchun.

options: Anna told that shorter weeks are good.
Anna argues that shorter weeks raise output.
Anna say shorter weeks are good.
Anna is right about shorter weeks.
quiz.why_uz: Argues that to‘g‘ri; told that xato, say da -s kerak, xulosa neytral bo‘lishi kerak.

quiz.q: You didn't hear the speaker. What is polite?
options: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that.
I'm not convinced that would work.
quiz.why_uz: I'm not convinced yumshoq, lekin aniq rad etish.

quiz.q: Someone interrupts you. A calm reply is:
options: Let me just finish this point.
quiz.why_uz: Let me just finish this point navbatni odob bilan saqlaydi.

quiz.q: 'The main point of disagreement is...' is used to:
Which verb is best for an unproven assertion?
